$comment: THE 1985 LANGUAGE ELEMENT STANDINGS, held once as data (kb/Work PB4993; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section
10.2): 1985 has one list, the obsolete language elements of §1985:C.1, which §1985:I.1.5.2.3 defines. One entry per
list item: its number `n`, the `terms` that name the element in a rule (each a whole word or phrase, as the text
spells it), the `sections` that specify it, and optional `section-terms` (extra terms for one of those sections only).
The item's name is the list's own text (element_standing.listed), never copied. A section is the element's
SPECIFICATION: its own clause, statement or module section, and each entry that specifies it beside current syntax
(an I-O-CONTROL paragraph, a file description entry, the Identification Division's organization, a statement whose
one phrase is obsolete). A rule elsewhere that refers to the element's effect is not part of it. OWN or SHARED is
derived from each section's heading (element_standing.own), never held here. `no-rule` states why an entry marks no
catalog rule, and is checked both ways. `remarks` names the sections whose obsolete-element sentence is not an
element's specification (here the level tables' Z notation). extract_rule_catalog.py --edition 1985 applies the
lists (each rule's `status`) and --check fails on any element_standing.findings.

remarks.why: the level tables' Z notation: a sentence about the notation, not an element

entries.no-rule: IV.4.1 states the substitution in prose; it holds no rule block

terms: ALL literal where the length of the literal is greater than one

entries.no-rule: VI.4.4 carries MEMORY SIZE only in its general format, which a section SHARED with OBJECT-COMPUTER never marks; no syntax or general rule names it
